scenario.prompt_to_agent:
PC3 and PC4 in Campus 2 VLAN 6 report their gateway (10.6.0.254)
no longer responds. Other Campus 2 PCs (PC1, PC2, dc_pc5 on
VLAN 5) are fine. Identify the misconfiguration.

injection.action: change br_v6 SVI IP from .254 to .200
injection.command:
ip addr del 10.6.0.254/24 dev br_v6
  ip addr add 10.6.0.200/24 dev br_v6

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: sshswitch br_v6 SVI IP address
Mechanism: PCs have their default route hard-coded to
  10.6.0.254 (the standard Cisco SVI VRRP-style address).
  sshswitch's br_v6 was reconfigured to 10.6.0.200, so
  ARP for 10.6.0.254 gets no reply — packets can't egress
  the subnet. The new address .200 IS reachable, but no host
  knows to use it.
Localization: sshswitch
Root cause: br_v6 SVI IP set to 10.6.0.200 instead of 10.6.0.254
Fix: re-set the IP — `ip addr del 10.6.0.200/24 dev br_v6 &&
  ip addr add 10.6.0.254/24 dev br_v6`
scenario.fix_spec:
re-set the IP — `ip addr del 10.6.0.200/24 dev br_v6 &&
  ip addr add 10.6.0.254/24 dev br_v6`
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: br_v6 SVI IP / VLAN 6 gateway IP

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** VLAN 6 gateway interface (`br_v6`) on sshswitch — the Layer 3 switch that provides inter-VLAN routing for Campus 2.

**Mechanism:** PC3 (10.6.0.3) and PC4 (10.6.0.4) have their default route set to 10.6.0.254. When they need to send traffic off-subnet, the kernel issues ARP requests for 10.6.0.254 on their eth0 interface. Because no device on the VLAN 6 segment owns that address, the ARP requests go unanswered and the kernel marks the neighbor entry as `FAILED`. Every attempted packet returns "Destination Host Unreachable" from the sending host itself — confirmed at 100% packet loss to all off-subnet destinations including the gateway IP directly.

**Localization:** sshswitch's `br_v6` bridge interface (the VLAN 6 SVI), which aggregates `eth0.6` (trunk to switch4) and `bond0.6` (uplink to router17). This interface is configured with `10.6.0.200/24` instead of the expected `10.6.0.254/24`. sshswitch's VLAN 5 interface (`br_v5`) is correctly set to `10.5.0.254/24`, explaining why VLAN 5 hosts (PC1, PC2, dc_pc5) on the same switch4 are completely unaffected. The anomaly is isolated to the VLAN 6 SVI address only.

**Root cause:** sshswitch's VLAN 6 gateway interface `br_v6` is assigned the wrong IP address — `10.6.0.200` instead of `10.6.0.254`.

**Fix:** Change the IP address of `br_v6` on sshswitch from `10.6.0.200/24` to `10.6.0.254/24`. This will make sshswitch respond to ARP requests from PC3 and PC4, restoring their default gateway and full external connectivity.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly identifies sshswitch (br_v6) as the localized faulty device in multiple sections.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly identifies the VLAN 6 gateway SVI (br_v6) and that its IP is set to 10.6.0.200 instead of the expected 10.6.0.254.
The proposed fix is to change br_v6 from 10.6.0.200/24 to 10.6.0.254/24, which exactly matches the expected remediation to restore ARP responses and gateway connectivity.

The log contains direct probes (pc pings showing 'Destination Host Unreachable'), ip/ARP checks on affected hosts, and the sshswitch interface listing showing br_v6 set to 10.6.0.200 — the agent's chain (PCs ARP for .254 → no reply because sshswitch has .200 → packets fail) is consistently supported by the observations.
